title: The kingdom handed over and the body's transformation
english: Here Paul calls the kingdom the ones being ruled—that is, his own flesh, which the Son handed over to the Father after making it better, no longer being ruled in the form of a servant but as being the flesh of the Word, which is the Son himself, having displayed the form of God in it. For then, when the Son has received back the glory he had before the world existed, they will be ruled by one king, the Father and the Son. Christ must therefore reign for the advancement of all, until all who are enemies because of sinning are placed under his feet, while he destroys every tyrannical authority. After that, death itself, the arch-evil one, is also destroyed, since every soul united to it undergoes death, which is united to wickedness.

Some commentators say these words were spoken against Greek mythology and deception—against those who claim the gods are father-killers—and that when the church is subjected, he himself is said to be subjected, appropriating to himself the persecutions, the sufferings, and the subjection of the church.

The Marcionites baptize living people on behalf of unillumined dead people, not knowing that baptism saves only the one who receives it. But the apostle calls our bodies dead, on whose behalf we are baptized; for by their own nature, without a soul, these do not live, but they have life from the souls that are present with them. Likewise Abraham also called the soulless body dead.
If the soul is not immortal, if the body is not raised, then risking danger for the sake of piety is futile.
As far as human reasoning goes, Paul says, "I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus; I would not have endured this for the truth, if the dead are not raised."

Do not be deceived, Corinthians, as though the rational soul does not endure. For those who deceive you corrupt others along with themselves, thinking that it is destroyed. Since bodies are wrapped around it, they say one must live luxuriously: for tomorrow we die, since there is no other life besides the visible one, as with irrational animals whose soul is destroyed together with the body, because it was sown together with it. So the worthless arguments that corrupt the minds of the simple must not be tolerated.

We must keep watch in our understanding, so that we do not happen to sin by consenting to the rotten deception about the resurrection. And "sober up" is well said—rightly so—since not all do this. For those who are clever at doing evil stay awake over harmful things and sober up for wicked ends, supposedly casting off the sleep of ignorance.

Paul, speaking in Christ, says to the one doubting about the resurrection of the dead, as to one who is unintelligent: Fool, if you doubt that the dead body of a human being is raised, know that the seeds you sow you cast into the ground dead, convinced that they would not change into plants unless sown dead. The body that is raised is different from the one you sowed: you cast a grain into the ground, but God raised up an ear of wheat. The argument about seeds answers one of the questions—the one that says, how are the dead raised? To the other question, with what kind of body do they come, he gives the proof by division, and dividing bodies into earthly and heavenly, he said that the glory of the raised human bodies is according to that of the heavenly sun, moon, and stars.

Like the glory of the lights and stars are not the bodies of all who are raised, but only those of the ones who have lived well and been self-controlled. For even if the bodies of the wicked are raised incorruptible, they are nevertheless deprived of the glory of the heavenly bodies. And it must be noted that the glory of the raised bodies is essential, just as is that of the lights.

Just as the rational soul, not being virtue or vice, is receptive of both of these, so also our body, not being corruption or incorruptibility, receives at different times the essential qualities that are placed in it. At any rate, it is not sown as corruption, nor is it raised as incorruptibility, but it is raised in incorruptibility. To what is sown in corruption follows being sown in weakness and dishonor and as a natural body; likewise, what is raised in incorruptibility corresponds to what is raised in power and glory and as a spiritual body.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Didymus is commenting on 1 Corinthians 15:24-43, explaining how Christ hands over the kingdom to the Father, refuting heretics on baptism for the dead, and arguing that the risen body is not the same perishable body that was sown.

title: The risen body is incorruptible by grace, not a fifth substance; the spiritual body and the change of the righteous
english: But when we speak of an incorruptible body, we are not speaking of a fifth substance, as some have supposed about the stars, which we say is always incorruptible. Rather, we call incorruptible what has become incorruptible from a corruptible state by the grace of God. In the same way, it is unchangeable and unalterable not in the sense of undergoing change—for it became incorruptible through change—but in the sense of enduring into long-lasting life, whether being punished or being honored. Since the body is sown from the intertwining of male with female, it is reasonable that dishonor and weakness will also attend it, since it is a natural body, being a body of a soul, the prior quality of which was corrupted in it. It is raised by the power of God, possessing incorruptibility and power and honor, shown to be a spiritual body, an instrument of the soul—no longer simply of the soul, but of the soul that has been raised by participation in the Holy Spirit and has, as it were, been changed into spirit. And since the soul that remains in the passions is such, the body of such a soul is also rightly called a natural body. But if the soul rises above the passionate condition, it becomes spiritual, and the body of such a soul, which is intertwined with it, is called a spiritual body. Since the soul, as it advances, ascends to the spiritual, Paul first said that the natural body exists, then the spiritual. And it must be understood that the body of those raised from the dead is made like the spiritual body of Christ, which came into being after the resurrection. Therefore we do not pay attention to those who say that the body is raised such as Adam had, a natural body. For the life of the first Adam prepared the human being to live as a living soul, but the life according to Christ is not into a living soul but into a life-giving spirit. And this spiritual making alive is proper to those raised from the dead. Paul fittingly said first and last man, not first and second man, so that we might learn that there have been some in between, in the conduct of the first and last man. Since the contemplation of the resurrection has depth of understanding, Paul reasonably says: "Behold, I tell you a mystery: we will all die and sleep, but only the righteous will be changed, shining like the sun." For only these, changing for the better in soul and body, will be changed. For it is not consistent to say, according to another reading that is circulated, "we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed," because of what is immediately added: "and we will be changed." For if all are changed, it is superfluous to say "and we will be changed." The dead will be raised with their body, which was formerly corruptible but will become incorruptible. But some say that here "we will be changed" means that we are some others besides the dead, who, they say, are raised with incorruptible bodies, while their souls are changed and altered for a better and more divine quality. Another says that the sinners are the dead, who are raised incorruptible so as to endure eternal punishments, while those who have lived according to virtue are changed from glory to glory. Now what is mortal is also corruptible, but not the reverse. Therefore the corruptible puts on incorruptibility, and the mortal puts on immortality, at the time of the resurrection of the dead. Just as when virtue is present, vice does not exist, so when immortality is present, death is destroyed. Therefore, when the mortal has put on immortality, death is defeated and swallowed up, so that it is said to it: "Where is your victory, by which you conquered and made people dead? Where is your sting, by which you wounded and were strong?" For it stings by casting sins into the thoughts of those struck by it, and it conquers those who sin in deed. The usage derives from Hosea, not in the same words: for instead of "your justice" the apostle said "victory" (Hosea 13:14 LXX, adapted by Paul). Since the enemy death has been destroyed, stand firm and remain steadfast in faith, working continually and without interruption the work commanded you by the Lord, taking courage without doubt, since your labor in the Lord is not in vain, an eternal reward being laid up for those who always do the work.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Didymus is expounding 1 Corinthians 15:44-58, explaining what Paul means by the natural body and the spiritual body, and correcting alternative readings of the resurrection and the change.

title: Closing exhortations, greetings, and the apostle's own hand
english: On the first day of the week, the Lord's resurrection day, store up among yourselves whatever your means can put aside, without grief and without compulsion, so that when I arrive I may find you ready to give, and so that when I have come there may not be a beginning of preparing the things for the fellowship (1 Corinthians 16:2).

He wrote this letter to the Corinthians from Ephesus. He says he is staying there for a good reason: a great and effectual opportunity has opened for him among his hearers (1 Corinthians 16:8-9). For this reason he had many opponents: wandering demons, and human sorcerers and deceivers. The wicked become many in their opposition whenever they see the word of faith growing strong in those who receive it. It is his custom to call the open opportunity for the word of godliness a door.

When those being taught are firm and immovable in godliness, teachers come to them without fear, not having any worry that there is slackness among the hearers. Therefore Paul says: watch yourselves, so that Timothy may be confident to come to you, not afraid that you may be turned aside (1 Corinthians 16:10-11). He used this meaning of fear also in the next letter, where he said: I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts may be corrupted (2 Corinthians 11:3).

Didymus comments: This Timothy, about whom I am writing these things, is one of God's genuine servants, doing the work of the Master in the same way as I do. Therefore let him not be despised among you, but let him be received genuinely with love, and also let him be sent on his way. For Paul says: I am waiting in Asia until he returns to me with the brothers.

Since Apollos was bishop of Corinth, he withdrew from them because of the divisions among them, and he was staying near Paul. And now, though urged, he did not travel with the letter. Paul states the reason he did not go: it was not his will (1 Corinthians 16:12). Then, to encourage them, he writes: he will come when he has opportunity, when you provide the opportunity for his visit to you, when there are no longer divisions among you.

To the one who keeps watch as he ought, giving no sleep to his eyes and no slumber to his eyelids, there follows standing firm in the faith. After this follows: act like men and be strong (1 Corinthians 16:13), as an athlete and soldier of Christ, doing everything with love toward God and neighbor.

They are called firstfruits either because they believed before the others, or because they excel in godliness, or because they are preeminent in family (1 Corinthians 16:15-16). Because of the humility present in them, they were not appointed by vote, but led to this by their own purpose, and they appointed themselves to service. Therefore submit to such people, having them as an image and pattern, so that you also may appoint yourselves to the service of the saints.
Together with Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus, being of the same purpose as he, supplied what was lacking among you, and they refreshed my spirit and yours (1 Corinthians 16:17-18).

The one who thinks and does the things of godliness refreshes the spirit of a holy person. For the spirit seeks good things, as it is in its nature. In the case of the wicked the human inner principle is called soul, but in the case of the holy it is called spirit, because it rises above in willing what is good. Therefore we must recognize those who live and think well by thinking and doing the same things. So also Didymus's teacher Origen holds that the spirit has something more than the soul in virtue, even though both spirit and soul exist.
Stirring them sufficiently to love, he writes: the churches of Asia greet you, and all the holy ones and brothers staying there (1 Corinthians 16:19).

So that they may not be deceived when some people write in the apostle's name, he makes this a sign of letters that are his and not his: that he has written with his own hand (1 Corinthians 16:21). And what is written by his holy right hand is this: if anyone does not love our Lord, let him be anathema. Maranatha (1 Corinthians 16:22). The one who does not keep his commandments does not love the Lord. Therefore this one is anathema, knowing that the Lord has come who judges the works of human beings, as Wisdom says in Proverbs 8:17: I love those who love me. But if he loves those who love him, consider what will overtake those who do not love him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Didymus is commenting on the final verses of 1 Corinthians 16, explaining Paul's instructions about the collection, his stay in Ephesus, Timothy and Apollos, the closing exhortations, greetings, and the curse on those who do not love the Lord.
